eligibility.quote: The timer as passed in there is not owned by the `Rate` object, it is owned by whatever is creating that (in this case, the Node is the one that calls `create_rate`).  Instead, the user should call `node.destroy_rate(rate)` to properly destroy a previously created Rate object.

Instead, the user should call `node.destroy_rate(rate)` to properly destroy a previously created Rate object.

loudness.quote: The CPU usage explodes and ros becomes laggy. I found that `Rate._timer` are not properly destroyed.

resolution.quote: Conclusion: Yes this works as intended and the CPU usage stays low.

notes: Agree with all fields. The consumer called Rate.destroy() instead of Node.destroy_rate(), causing uncancelled timers in rclpy to leak and explode CPU usage.
